resources.string: Help & troubleshooting
Short answers to what people ask most. Each one ends where you can fix it.
Parley\'s call screen doesn\'t show

Calls show on Parley\'s own screen only while Parley is your default phone app. Without it, Parley still lists your calls and contacts, and your old phone app answers calls.\n\nIf Android says \"Restricted setting\", Parley was installed from a file: open App info, tap ⋮ › Allow restricted settings, then try again.
Default phone app
A call didn\'t ring

Your blocking rules, the spam lists or a Situation may have kept it quiet. Test a call shows what your rules would do with any number, and replays last week\'s calls so you can see which rule stopped one. On a number\'s page in Recents, \"Why it rang, or didn\'t\" says the same for one call.
Why Parley doesn\'t record calls

On today\'s Android (10 to 16), an app can\'t capture the other person\'s voice during a call. That audio is closed to apps — only your phone maker\'s own dialer or the system can reach it. The microphone is muted to apps during a call too, so the \"speakerphone and microphone\" trick records only a poor, one-sided version and plays both sides aloud to the room. The ways around this — an accessibility service, or rooting the phone — are unsafe or banned from app stores, and are the same route stalkerware uses, so Parley won\'t ship them. Recording a call can also be against the law where you are unless everyone agrees.\n\nWhat Parley keeps instead is a written record of what was said and agreed, with no audio. A Call receipt and a call record are coming. For now, Case files hold the calls, hold times and reference numbers for a bank or other service, and notes keep the rest. If you truly need the audio, your phone maker\'s own Phone app records in some countries and tells both sides.
Calls are quiet while a Situation is on

A Situation (Driving, Meeting, Night, Travelling or your own) sets who may ring while it\'s on. The chip above the tabs shows which one is on and turns it off in one tap. Turning it off puts every setting back as it was. To let more people ring during one, open it and choose who may ring.
I\'m waiting for a call from a number I don\'t know

A delivery, a doctor or a new job may call from a number you haven\'t saved. Expecting a call lets unknown callers ring for a while, then your usual rules come back on their own. Numbers you blocked stay blocked.
Missed calls and reminders don\'t show

Android may have turned off Parley\'s notifications, or one of their kinds. Check that Parley\'s notifications are allowed, Missed calls among them. On the lock screen, Parley shows only \"Missed call\" or \"Reminder\" until you unlock, as you chose.
Notification settings
A flashing light when the phone rings

Parley doesn\'t add a flash of its own. Android has one built in that works for every app: open Settings › Accessibility › Flash notifications and turn on the camera flash, the screen flash, or both. Because it\'s Android\'s own, it keeps working whether or not Parley is your phone app. Whether incoming calls flash can vary by phone.
Reminders, backups or Situations come late

To save battery, some phones stop apps that work in the background. Parley does little in the background, but scheduled backups, reminders and a Situation\'s end time need it. Let Parley run without battery limits, and on some phones also allow it to start on its own.
Battery optimisation
A contact disappeared after Archive

Archive takes a contact out of your address book and other apps, while Parley keeps them sealed and still names their calls. Nothing is lost. Archived contacts are listed together, and Unarchive puts one back in your address book.
I deleted or changed a contact by mistake
History & undo keeps 30 days of changes to your contacts: deletes, edits and merges. Find the change and tap Undo. Older versions are in the daily snapshots, on the same screen.
I\'m moving to a new phone

On this phone, open Encrypted backups and choose Move to a new phone, or Back up now. Copy the backup to the new phone, install Parley there and choose \"From another phone with Parley? Restore a backup\" on the first screen. Private contacts, notes, Situations and settings come along.
Parley\'s screens look empty, or show an error

If a list looks empty when it shouldn\'t, or opening something shows an error, Check Parley\'s data looks over everything Parley keeps sealed on this phone and tells you, in plain words, what it can and can\'t read. It only looks: it never changes, moves or deletes anything, so it can\'t make things worse. Anything it can\'t read is left exactly as it is, and you can put it back from a backup. This is rare — it can follow a phone update that lost Parley\'s secure keys, or restoring app data the wrong way.
Something else isn\'t working
Export diagnostics makes a short report about your phone and Parley\'s settings, with no names, numbers or notes in it. You choose whether to share it, and with whom.

Give a label an end: a move, a hospital stay, a project or a trip. When it ends, Parley asks once what to do with it, such as keep the label as it is or archive its people. Nothing changes until you choose. Open a label, then choose Give it an end.

Something to bring up with someone: ask about the trip, return the book. It shows on the call screen when you next call them or they call you, and you tick it off there. Add one from a contact\'s page or a number\'s page, or share text to Parley and choose Add to talk about with….

Members of a label you share, such as Family, can share their block and scam verdicts. Only coded fingerprints of numbers are shared: no names and no notes. A number is warned about, silenced or blocked, as you choose for that label, and never if it\'s a saved contact or an emergency number. Open a shared label, then Family spam shield.

Can\'t talk now? Choose Decline & promise a time on a ringing call, Promise a time… under Remind me on a missed call or after a call, or on Remind me to call. Pick a time, in their time if their clock differs, and your messaging app opens with \"I\'ll call you back at 15:30.\" for you to send. Parley reminds you then, from To call, and if they ring first the call screen says what you promised.

Waiting for a hospital or a bank to call you back? Choose They\'ll call me back… under Remind me after a call, or on Remind me to call, and say by when. Until then their call rings through, from any number if you choose, and Parley won\'t say the number never calls you. If they haven\'t called by then, To call says so.

At the top of Recents, Next up shows at most three things that matter now: the calls you owe (and times you said you\'d call), today\'s birthdays and anniversaries, someone in your Circle at the hours they\'re usually free, and a Chapter ending this week. Each line has one action. Nothing shows when nothing is due. After a call with someone in your Circle, Anything to remember? can set your next catch-up, which waits in To call.

Life changes how often you need to be in touch: someone in hospital, a new baby, a friend going through a hard time. In someone\'s keep-in-touch rhythm, For a while… sets a closer rhythm, like every 3 days, until a date or for some weeks. Your Circle shows it (“Every 3 days · until 30 Nov”), and the usual rhythm comes back by itself, with one line in the next weekly digest. For a group, give a label an end (a Chapter) and switch on Keep in touch with everyone here: its people get that rhythm while the Chapter runs.
Quieter than usual

Drifting apart happens quietly. Parley compares the last 6 months with the year before, from your own calls and the chats you start from Parley. When you used to talk often (at least 6 times before) and now talk at least half as often, the weekly digest may say so, for one person at most a week: “You and Marco used to talk about every week; since April it\'s been about every month.” Call, Add to your Circle, or They\'re fine, which keeps Parley quiet about them for a year. Nothing is stored but that choice, and it never shows after a duress unlock.
Keep in touch with everyone in a label

On a label\'s page, Keep in touch with everyone here sets a rhythm; switch it on and everyone in the label is in your Circle (“In your Circle via Family”). A rhythm of their own always wins, and each person counts once, at the closest rhythm. Switching it off takes out only those who were in through the label. Add everyone to Favourites stars everyone in the label after showing you who; Undo unstars exactly them.

Touch and hold an empty spot on your home screen, choose Widgets, then Parley\'s Situations. At one cell it is one switch: for the Situation on now, or else the one you turn on most. Wider, it shows a row of your Situations, the one on filled; two cells high, it also says which is on. A tap turns a Situation on until you turn it off (or another one on), just like the Quick Settings tile, and turning it off puts back what you had. Nothing changes while the phone is locked. Situations you add, rename or delete show up on the widget by themselves.

Once a year is over, it\'s good to look back. On the People card in Call insights, Your year shows any year Parley has history for: how often you were in touch, who most, who you grew closer to and who got quieter (compared with the year before, among people you talked to at least 4 times), the longest gap with someone in your Circle, the occasions you acknowledged, and calls against chats started from Parley. It is worked out when you open it and nothing is kept. Early in January the weekly digest offers last year once. Older years can be thin: Parley knows the calls Android\'s call log kept. It never shows after a duress unlock.
